guide.summary: Private app on your own workspace (self-serve, wait none); Public app for other Intercom customers (app review).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Private app on your own workspace (self-serve, wait none). Hardest: Public app for other Intercom customers (app review).

composio.note: Composio provides a managed OAuth app for Intercom, fine for prototypes. For launch with your own branding, create a custom auth config with your own client ID and secret.

need_own_app.answer: Not for prototypes, since Composio provides a managed Intercom OAuth app. For launch, a own app gives your branding on the consent screen, your chosen scopes, dedicated quota, and shorter polling intervals.
reasons: Consent screen shows Composio's name with managed apps
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users
Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval
Default scopes may not cover what you need

prerequisites.title: Developer Hub app with OAuth enabled
prerequisites.detail: Tick Use OAuth on the Authentication page; client ID and secret are on the Basic Information page.

prerequisites.title: HTTPS redirect URL
prerequisites.detail: Redirect URLs must be HTTPS. Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.

prerequisites.title: Test account or setup instructions
prerequisites.detail: If your service needs an account, provide test credentials or setup instructions in the description.

steps.title: Create app and enable OAuth
steps.detail: Sign in to the Developer Hub, create the app and tick Use OAuth.
steps.done_when: Client ID and secret visible on Basic Information page.

steps.title: Draft minimal scope list
steps.detail: Choose only the scopes the agent's use case needs and write a justification for each.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create an auth config via Composio's API with your client ID and secret; copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard into the Developer Hub.

steps.title: Record OAuth demo video
steps.detail: Show install with full client_id and state in the OAuth URL, app functionality, and uninstall.

steps.title: Prepare description and listing
steps.detail: Write the description; for listing, prepare the icon, images, categories and Start Guide.

steps.title: Submit for review
steps.detail: Submit from the Test and publish section of the Developer Hub.

steps.title: Wait for Intercom review
steps.detail: Review can take up to seven business days; resubmissions take as long.

traps.title: Over-privileged scopes cause rejection
traps.detail: This is the most common reason for initial rejection. You may be asked to adjust scopes and resubmit.

traps.title: Broken links or wrong image format
traps.detail: Broken installation links cause rejection, as do images not in marketing format.

traps.title: Redirect URL choice only after approval
traps.detail: Choosing among multiple redirect URLs, including testing ones, is possible only after approval.

traps.title: Region-specific authorization hosts
traps.detail: Intercom hosts workspaces in three regions, each with its own authorization host.

blockers.symptom: Review asks you to adjust scopes
blockers.what_it_means: Requested scopes exceed what the app currently does.
blockers.agent_can_help: Compare scopes to features and propose a reduced list.

blockers.symptom: No review response after the stated window
blockers.what_it_means: Reviews can run longer than stated; one forum post reports 15 days.
